resumeLine: Designed a feature flag service with a 50ms p99 read path backed by an in-process cache.

claims.quote: feature flag service with a 50ms p99 read path

answers.text: Reads hit an in-process map, so the p99 is dominated by the map lookup rather than the store. The 50ms figure is the read path including the surrounding handler.
It caches flags in memory so reads are fast.
We cached it the usual way.
The cache has no TTL and no invalidation, so a flag flipped in the store never reaches a running process until it restarts. That is the part I would change.
The cache keeps flags in memory and refreshes them.

seededDefects.description: The cache has no TTL and no invalidation path, so a flag flip never reaches a running process.
A failed refresh silently keeps serving stale values with no signal that the data is old.
